title: Boys Don't Need Looksmaxxing! They Need Purpose.
author: Hirsi Ali, Ayaan
summary: The rise of 'looksmaxxing'—the systematic optimization of male physical appearance through grooming, diet, and cosmetic procedures—is not merely a social media trend but a symptom of Western civilization's abandonment of the imago Dei as the basis for human worth. When a culture stops telling young men they are made in the image of God, it removes the only framework capable of grounding dignity in something deeper than appearance, and the internet fills the vacuum with algorithmic self-evaluation: facial ratios, symmetry scores, and hierarchical rankings. The article critiques looksmaxxing's competitive logic as fundamentally dehumanizing—training men to rank others before learning their names, reducing romance to a market strategy, and treating the body as a product. Physical attraction matters, the author concedes, but marriages and communities are built on character, loyalty, faith, and shared purpose. The solution is not mockery but recovery of the older tradition: forming boys in the conviction that courage, integrity, and faithfulness—not facial symmetry—are the foundations of a life worth living.
points: Looksmaxxing is a symptom of moral vacuity, not just a social media pathology. When civilization abandons the imago Dei as the basis of human worth, it removes the only framework capable of grounding dignity in something deeper than appearance—and algorithmic self-evaluation rushes in to replace it with followers, scores, and rankings.

The competitive logic of looksmaxxing is corrosive to the relational goods it claims to pursue. By treating attraction as a mathematical formula, it trains young men in self-obsession and comparison at precisely the stage of life when they most need to learn loyalty, generosity, and how to love—skills built on far deeper foundations than facial symmetry.

The answer is not critique but formation. Young men need to be positively shaped by the older tradition—that character, discipline, and purpose sustain marriages and communities—not simply told looksmaxxing is wrong. A man who lives with integrity, works hard, and loves faithfully will always be more attractive than a sculpted jawline.
quotes: This is what a civilization looks like when it loses its language of human dignity. It was once grounded in a moral vision: the belief that every person is made in the imago Dei.

The logic of looksmaxxing is the logic of the competitive marketplace: you are a product, your value is measurable, and you are probably deficient. For young men already adrift from any stronger account of who they are, this message lands without friction.
Looksmaxxing inverts this: it trains young men to rank every male they encounter before they have learned his name.

Physical attraction matters, of course. But anyone who has observed real relationships knows that marriages, families, and lifelong partnerships are built on far deeper foundations: character, loyalty, kindness, humour, faith, and shared vision and purpose.
A man who lives with integrity, who cares for others, who works hard, who loves faithfully has, and will, always be more attractive than any sculpted jawline.
